name: Woodlake Park
note: Family-run since 1978, 2.5 mi south of Lake City on Hwy 149 at the foot of Slumgullion Pass. River Loop along the Lake Fork of the Gunnison, Forest Loop under pines and aspens; also cabins, bunkhouses and riverside tent sites. No generators. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Opens the Friday before Memorial Day; the site shows it open through September 30.
field_notes.Booking: Book by calling the office, 970-901-6713 (daily 9-5 MT); the online stay-request form is paused. A deposit is taken and is non-refundable; cancel at least 2 weeks ahead, by phone. No check-in after dark or after 8 PM.
field_notes.Sites: River Loop 28 sites along the Lake Fork, Forest Loop 22 under pines and aspens. The site map lists 52 RV sites (30 River, 22 Forest), 26-96 ft, nearly all 35 ft or more. Site assignments are made by the office to fit the rig; a loop or site can be requested, not guaranteed.

name: Carter Lake - Eagle Campground
note: Larimer County campground at the north end of Carter Lake, west of Loveland; the loop runs from a hill above the lake (E01-E22, with lake views) down into a meadow below the dam (E23-E49, no view). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: A reservation and a park entrance permit are required before setting up at any site; a no-show unannounced within 24 hours may lose the site (call 970-619-4570). Check-in noon, check-out 11 am. One wheeled camping unit per site.
field_notes.Fees: Electric sites April-September: $35 weeknights, $45 weekends, $55 holidays; October-March $25-30. Plus the $8.75 reservation fee and a daily entrance permit ($10 a vehicle, $20 with a trailered boat).
field_notes.Sites: 47 50-amp electric sites (E02-E49 without E34), 43 of them pull-through, listed for vehicles 32-80 ft (most 40-50). E01-E22 sit on a hill overlooking the lake; E23-E49 are in a meadow below the dam with no lake view.

name: Hermit Park Open Space
note: Larimer County open space ~2 mi SE of Estes Park, 7,880-8,964 ft, ponderosa forest and meadows; no water recreation on site (Lake Estes is 3 mi away). Bobcat (campground #2) is the RV campground; Hermit's Hollow (#1) sites cap at 20 ft, Kruger (#3) is equestrian. --Claude

Booking: min stay 2 nights on weekends (May - mid-October)

field_notes.Season: 'Hermit Park closes for the season Dec 20-Mar 1' (weather dependent); the county's park page says 'open March through mid December'.
field_notes.Booking: Larimer County's ReserveAmerica site (larimercamping.com) or 1-800-397-7795; same-day bookings online 24/7 or at the park office, and QR codes at sites for after-hours walk-ups, but 'Campers MUST make a reservation and purchase a park entrance permit BEFORE setting up'. Two-night minimum for weekend dates May through mid-October at Hermit Park; 14 nights in any 30 days across the county system. Park office 970-619-4570.
field_notes.Fees: Hermit Park non-electric campsite (March-December): $35 a night weekdays, $45 weekends, $50 holidays; equestrian sites (May-September) $45/$60/$65. $8.75 reservation fee per stay. Daily entrance permit $10 per vehicle (valid 24 hours), or a Larimer County annual permit.
field_notes.Sites: 91 campsites in four campgrounds plus 13 camper cabins and a group pavilion: Bobcat (#2) 39 drive-in sites, max vehicle 25-45 ft (8 at 40 ft, 2 at 45 ft; 6 pull-throughs); Hermit's Hollow (#1) 42 sites, 30 drive-in all capped at 20 ft and 12 hike-in; Granite Gulch (#4) 5 sites, 20-35 ft; Kruger Equestrian (#3) 5 horse sites with corrals, 40-60 ft.

name: Molas Lake Park & Campground
note: Town-of-Silverton-run high-alpine park at ~10,508 ft on US-550 (Million Dollar Hwy) at a stocked 25-acre lake. Generators only in the Ultra RV and Rock Cliff RV sites, 8 AM-8 PM; no swimming. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Online through the Town of Silverton's WebReserv calendar, by site number within a site type; the season's reservations open January 1. Sells out most of the summer. Cancel within 90 days of booking and 7+ days before arrival for a 50% refund; otherwise no refund. Check-in 1 p.m., check-out 11 a.m.
field_notes.Fees: Small RV/Tent and Rock Cliff Standard RV sites $50, Premium Water View $70, Lake-View Ultra RV $90 a night, plus 10.4% tax. Rates rise 50% over the July 4th and Labor Day holiday periods ($75 / $105 / $135).
field_notes.Sites: The home page says 62 campsites (the FAQ says 58). The 2026 site sheet describes 4 Lake-View Ultra RV and 8 Rock Cliff Standard RV sites (50-57, all back-in) that take RVs of any size, 29 Small RV/Tent and 15 Premium Water View sites mostly limited to motorhomes up to 23 ft or trailers up to 20 ft, some 14-15 ft and some tent-only. Site 2 is a pull-through for RVs up to 23 ft.

name: Pinewood Reservoir Campground
note: Larimer County campground on the northeast end of Pinewood Reservoir west of Carter Lake (~6,580 ft), part of the Colorado-Big Thompson Project. The county warns the only access is a narrow 4-mile paved road with 8-10% grades and that most sites are small, not recommended for larger RVs and motorhomes. Drinking water runs April-August only; the nearest frost-free spigot is at Flatiron Campground, 4 miles east. Boat ramp closed: hand-launched craft only, no swimming. A daily vehicle entrance permit is required on top of the camping fee. --Claude

Booking: min stay 2 nights on weekends (April - September)

field_notes.Booking: Larimer County's ReserveAmerica site (larimercamping.com) or 1-800-397-7795, same day up to 180 days ahead. March-October, sites not reserved become first-come that day for people at the park (same-day reservations at the visitor centers); November-February a reservation and a park entrance permit must be bought online before setting up. 14 nights in any 30 across the county system. Check-in noon, check-out 11 a.m.; a no-show unannounced within 24 hours may lose the site (970-619-4570).
field_notes.Fees: Larimer County: electric sites $35 a night weekdays, $45 weekends, $55 holidays (April-September), $25-30 October-March; non-electric $25-35; daily entrance permit required in addition; $8.75 reservation fee. Read 2026-10-16.
field_notes.Sites: 16 drive-in electric sites (P01-P16) and 11 walk-in tent sites (P17-P27) on the booking site; the county's description says 15 electric and 12 walk-in. Max vehicle length by site: 55 (P05, P07, P16), 45 (P09), 40 (P01), 30-35 for most, 15 (P08). Pull-throughs P01-P04, P06, P08, P10-P15. One wheeled camping unit per site.

name: Dead Timber State Recreation Area
note: NGPC recreation area on a Logan Creek/Elkhorn oxbow off US 275, ~4 mi north of Scribner, beside Powder Horn WMA. Electric sites in a loop at the south end of the oxbow; the four primitive sites have been closed by flood damage. Self-pay envelopes. Primitive restrooms. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Electric sites $25 a night in season, $5 less mid-October through April; the four primitive sites ($10) are closed by flood damage. Pay by envelope at the self-service box. Plus tax and a park entry permit ($7 a day for a Nebraska vehicle, $14 otherwise; $35 / $70 a year).

name: Lake Minatare State Recreation Area - Lake View Campground
note: NGPC SRA on the 2,158-acre Lake Minatare NE of Scottsbluff. Lake View campground runs along the west arm on the peninsula by the office: paved back-ins in a cottonwood belt, part bookable online, the rest first come. West Wind has basic sites, and there is non-designated beach and primitive camping. The Butte View campground across the lake is its own entry. Plains Lighthouse, boat ramps. A wildlife refuge, closed to all public access October 15 - January 15. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Closed to all public access October 15 - January 15 (wildlife refuge).
field_notes.Fees: In season: primitive $10, basic $15, electric plus $30 a night (ReserveAmerica, June 2027); $5 less in the off-season except primitive. The park is closed October 15 - January 15. Plus tax.
field_notes.Sites: 52 electric plus sites (50 A, paved back-ins; ReserveAmerica books 37, 37-63 ft, most 46-55), plus West Wind basic sites and non-designated primitive and beach camping.

name: Lone Eagle Campground - Lake McConaughy SRA
note: Lone Eagle campground of Lake McConaughy SRA, on the north shore off Shoreline Road (Arthur Bay Gate 2 or Sandy Beach Gate 4 off Highway 92): a paved loop of full hookup back-ins, its south-west row behind a line of trees above the wide sand beach. Beach camping on the sand is separate and booked 30 days ahead. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: All camping at Lake McConaughy is by advance reservation only: 180 days ahead for designated sites, 30 days for beach camping.
field_notes.Fees: Full hookup $35 Sunday-Wednesday, $40 Thursday-Saturday (May 21 - September 12), $30 the rest of the year. Plus tax.
field_notes.Sites: 84 full hookup sites, 50 A, paved 60-ft back-ins.

name: Niobrara State Park
note: State park on the bluffs at the Niobrara-Missouri confluence, NE Nebraska. The modern campground is one paved loop with an inner row, east of the park road below the bluffs; the east row backs onto a thick tree belt along a river backwater, with no water view. Carpets on the asphalt pads only. Tent camping on a separate hilly one-way loop. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Camping, including electric sites, all year; modern restrooms, showers and water run about May to mid-October, with a winter rate when they are closed.
field_notes.Fees: Electric Plus sites $30 a night in season, $25 off-season (mid-October through April); the one full-hookup site $35. The basic sites are the tent area. Plus tax, the $8.50 reservation fee when booked online, and a park entry permit ($7 a day for a Nebraska vehicle, $14 otherwise; $35 / $70 a year).
field_notes.Sites: Modern Campground sites 1-76 plus sites 77-81; reservable sites are 45-68 ft back-ins. Tent sites line a separate hilly one-way loop.

name: Summit Lake State Recreation Area
note: SRA on a 190-acre lake 3 mi west of Tekamah. Two loops off the park road: Muskrat (sites 02-22) and Eckdahl (25-43, on the slope above the swim beach and boat ramps). 43 Electric Plus sites and 25 basic non-electric sites. Water from spigots; ReserveAmerica lists a water hookup at sites 28 and 39 only. Primitive restrooms, swim beach. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: 31 of the 43 Electric Plus sites are on ReserveAmerica; the rest of the electric sites and the non-electric sites are first come. Reservations must be made at least a day ahead; reservations were taken through Nov 15 2026 (read 2026-11-05).
field_notes.Fees: In season: basic $15, electric $25, electric plus $30 a night; $5 less mid-October through April. Plus tax, the $8.50 reservation fee when booked online, and a park entry permit ($7 a day for a Nebraska vehicle, $14 otherwise; $35 / $70 a year). Nebraska Game and Parks' camping rates grid ('These rates are consistent across all parks'), matched on its booking site for June 2027 nights, read 2026-10-12.

name: Swanson Reservoir SRA - Spring Canyon Campground
note: Modern electric loop at Swanson Reservoir SRA near Trenton: 47 RV sites with 20/30/50-amp hookups, modern restrooms and showers, two dump stations; shaded sites set back in the canyon (the sandy-beach primitive areas are separate loops). Reservable on ReserveAmerica up to 180 days ahead (25 Spring Canyon sites listed there in 2026). Park entry permit required. --Claude

field_notes.Season: ReserveAmerica's Swanson SRA campground facility (Lake View, Macklin Bay and Spring Canyon loops) says 'Status: Open year round', with sites bookable through the winter. Winter water/showerhouse service is not stated.
field_notes.Booking: ReserveAmerica lists 25 Spring Canyon sites (23 electric, 2 basic; site numbers 1-42 with gaps), bookable up to 180 days ahead and at least 1 day before arrival. Whether the unlisted site numbers are first-come is not stated on the booking site.
field_notes.Fees: In season: basic $15, electric plus $30, primitive $10 a night; $5 less mid-October through April (primitive $10 all year). Plus tax, the $8.50 reservation fee when booked online, and a park entry permit ($7 a day for a Nebraska vehicle, $14 otherwise; $35 / $70 a year). Nebraska Game and Parks' camping rates grid ('These rates are consistent across all parks'), matched on its booking site for June 2027 nights, read 2026-10-12.

name: Bessey Recreation Complex
note: Nebraska National Forest (Bessey Ranger District) campground at Halsey, in the historic hand-planted Bessey forest. Loops of pine-shaded pads, most with electric; a group site and tent-only sites besides. Showers and flush restroom mid-May to mid-October; winter water only at the recreation building. The Middle Loup River (tubing, canoeing) and a 7-acre stocked pond are nearby, but the loops sit back in the trees, not on the water. ATVs may ride from the sites to the trailhead. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Showers and the flush restroom run mid-May to mid-October; in winter water only at the recreation building.
field_notes.Booking: About half the sites reservable from mid-May to mid-October; the rest, and every site in winter, first come (payable in the Recreation.gov app).
field_notes.Fees: Single site $15 a night non-electric, $20 electric (Forest Service page and recreation.gov rate table); day use $5 a vehicle.

name: Adams County Fairgrounds
note: Adams County Fairgrounds camping at 947 South Baltimore, Hastings, with 396 hookup sites: 20 back-in full-service sites south of the grandstands (upgraded to 50/30 amp in 2021), 86 water-and-electric and 290 electric-only, plus a tent field, a shower house and a dump station at the entrance that takes free-will donations.  The campground is seasonal, opening and closing with the weather, and closes to the public during several fairground events.  RV stays are limited to three weeks and tent stays to one, and campfires aren't allowed. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Opening and closing dates depend on the weather, and the campground closes to the public during several fairground events.
field_notes.Fees: Set Your Sites prices for a 2027-05-12 night (read 2026-11-05): $30 for every electric and water-and-electric site, $35 for a full-service site. Books online through Set Your Sites or by phone.

name: Ag Park (Platte County Fairgrounds)
note: Platte County Agricultural Society fairgrounds in Columbus. One RV site type is unavailable during carnival week and another offers extended stays; horse stalls on the grounds. Reviewers mention frequent passing trains and a somewhat run-down feel. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Read on the Campspot marketplace: one night for 2 adults, site rate before tax, every RV site type a 23-ft rig fits (Standard RV Site, Standard RV Site: Extended Stay Option and Standard RV Site: Unavailable During Carnival Week). October 2026: $35, Tuesday and Saturday alike. June 2027 isn't open for booking yet. Campspot adds its own booking fee at checkout (3%, at least $3). Read 2026-10-13.

name: Beck Memorial Park
note: Village of Decatur park on the Missouri River at the edge of town (lower camping area along the river, upper loop by the ballfields); boat ramp and fish-cleaning station. A 2021 reviewer found it full of long-term campers who 'book for a couple months at a time', so call ahead in season. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $25 a night (RV Life review, October 2025). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: CAMPER-REPORTED RATE (RV Life review, stay 10/2025): $25 a night for a back-in travel-trailer site with power and water, no sewer. The Village of Decatur has no web page of its own; call to confirm.

name: Christensen Field - Fremont Parks & Recreation
note: City of Fremont campground at the Christensen Field complex, outside the Main Arena. The West Campground is open to the public; the East Campground's 20 pedestals are for special events only. Campers may have to move or leave for a scheduled event. No tents. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Opens between April 1 and Memorial Day, with the first scheduled special event; the Nov 1 closing is subject to weather.
field_notes.Booking: Register within an hour of taking a site, and by 4 pm each day unless the whole stay is paid in advance. 14 consecutive days per calendar year; longer needs the Parks and Recreation Office's approval (402-727-2634). Sites are held for scheduled events, so campers may have to move or leave.
field_notes.Fees: City of Fremont: $25 a night, paid by envelope at the drop-box (cash or check) or at the Parks and Recreation Office; a $10 late charge if not registered within an hour. A camper paid $25 in June 2026.

name: Deshler City Park Campground
note: City of Deshler campground in Washington Park (Park St east of 4th St) by the municipal pool and ballfields; ~10-12 sites along the lot. The parallel-park layout is a little confusing and a long rig may need to unhook, but a 23-ft Class C fits. The low part of the park floods in heavy rain: in 2020 city workers moved a camper up the hill ahead of a storm. Dump station in town, not at the park. Paved walking path, horseshoes, sand volleyball. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: first night free, then $15 (July 2025). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: CAMPER-REPORTED RATE (Campendium, reported 7/8/2025): '1 night free, $15/day after that. QR code to make payments.' The City of Deshler has no web page; Thayer County's tourism page still calls the hook-ups free. Call the city (402-365-4260) to confirm.

name: Genoa City Park Campground
note: City of Genoa park (Nance County). A few gravel/grass sites with 30-amp electric and water on the camping loop at the south side of the park, beside the pool and ball fields; a wooded creek channel runs beyond the loop road. Pay at the city offices. --Claude  CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $25 a night in July 2024 (RV Life review: the city raised it from $10); the city's pages post no rate (2026-10-11). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: $25 a night per a camper's July 2024 report (the city had raised it from $10); the city's pages post no rate. Paid at the city offices.

name: Kirkman's Cove Recreation Area
note: Nemaha NRD recreation area on 160-acre Kirkman's Cove Lake, 2.5 mi W and 0.5 mi N of Humboldt. Two camping areas with separate entrances: the Beach Entrance loop off 715 Road on the east shore (all the electric pads, a few non-electric pads, tent camping and the sand swimming beach), and the non-electric pads off the Main Entrance from Hwy 4 on the southwest shore, by the playground and the boat ramp. A few pads on the west side of the Beach Entrance loop face the lake across open lawn. Boat ramp and dock, kayak launch (new 2026), 9-hole golf course adjacent. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: First come, first served; 'Reserving campsites is prohibited.' Pay within 30 minutes of arrival by scanning the QR code sign at the campsite (Set Your Sites, card only); Set Your Sites shows live availability on a map. Only RVs/campers on RV pads and they must be attended. Tents move every 7 days; extensions past 14 days need the manager's written permission.
field_notes.Fees: Primitive (non-electric) RV pads and tent camping $5 a night, electric RV pads $20 (NRD page and Set Your Sites). A Nemaha NRD park permit is required on top: $5 daily, $15 annual, $23 for a two-vehicle annual bundle; Nebraska state park permits are not valid.
field_notes.Sites: 32 RV pads: 16 electric and 4 non-electric in the Beach Entrance loop on the east shore, and 12 non-electric pads off the Main Entrance on the southwest shore (8 by the playground, 4 by the boat ramp), plus four tent camping areas. The NRD's rules cap any camper unit at 102 inches wide and 40 ft long. Tents are not allowed on RV pads.

name: Lynch RV Park
note: Village of Lynch RV park on the south side of town (4th St & Railroad Ave), a short walk from the main street; Ponca Creek is beyond the trees to the south-east. Back-in gravel pads in grass with tables and fire pits, a covered picnic area. Pay at a bar downtown or call for pickup; Grass can be long and neighbouring dogs noisy (2024 review). CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $25 a night in July 2024 (The Dyrt and Campendium reviews); the village has no web page (2026-11-05). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Camper-reported: $25 a night with full hookups (The Dyrt review, July 2024; Campendium, July 2024). Pay at a bar downtown or call for pickup. The village posts no rate.

name: South Park Campground
note: City of Franklin's small RV park at Hwy 10 & 15th Ave, a paved lot with hookups beside the town park, pool and playground. Pay the city (City Hall phone). Next to Hwy 10, so trucks pass at night. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $20 a night in October 2024 (RV Life review); the city has no web page about the campground (2026-11-05). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Camper-reported: an RV Life reviewer paid $20 a night with a fifth wheel in October 2024. The City of Franklin has no page about the campground and posts no rate.

name: Valentine City Park
note: City of Valentine 40-acre park on North Main Street, just outside town, along Minnechaduza Creek. Primitive camping on undesignated gravel pull-offs beside the park road; low oak branches (a 32-ft Class C got through in 2023). Water spigots around the park; water and restrooms typically shut off in the off-season. No dump station noted. Mill Pond across the road is stocked. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $5 (9/2024) and $10 (4/2024) a night, self-pay drop box (RV Life reviews); no city page posts a rate. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Camper-reported: $5 (9/2024) and $10 (4/2024) a night, self-pay. No city page posts a rate.

name: York County Fairgrounds Campground
note: York County fairgrounds at 2345 Nebraska Ave, with camping open to the public outside fair week as well. Gridded angled pull-in pads; a dump site nearby. Fair-week spots are booked through the county extension office. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Water and electric sites: $15 with 30-amp, $20 with 50-amp; tents $5. Fair week $125 a spot, booked through the county extension office.

name: I-80 Lakeside Campground
note: Campground on a private ~10-acre lake between I-80 (Exit 179) and the Platte River at North Platte. Pull-throughs for any size RV, plus primitive and tent areas along the lake. Swimming beaches, catch-and-release fishing with no permit needed, and kayak and paddle-boat rentals. Off-season (Oct 1-Apr 14) is self-registration at the office dropbox, with water only at sites H-X and no showers. Reservations by phone with a $10 deposit. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Office, showers and laundry open April 15-September 30; off-season self-registration with electric at all sites and water only at sites H-X.
field_notes.Fees: Water + electric $35, full hookup $41, pre-tax; 50 amp $3 extra; off-season (Oct-Apr 14) flat $35; NebraskaLand Days rates higher.

name: Jeske's Over The Hill Campground
note: Small private campground next to Carhenge north of Alliance, with views across open country. All pull-through sites on a slight hill in full sun; most need side-to-side levelling, and hookups are spread out at many sites. Self check-in kiosk, pay cash in an envelope. Full-hookup, water-only and no-hookup sites, 3rd consecutive night half price. Campers report no bathhouse; porta-johns for tents. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: No hookup (water available) $17, water only $27, full hookup $35 a night; 3rd consecutive night half price; open all year.
